title: Give the route class a procedure: four playbooks in one home, cited not copied
action:
Add ONE new section `## Class playbooks` to skills/bee-planning/references/planning-reference.md — no new file (planning-reference.md:6 says 'Fold, don't fan out', and bee-planning/SKILL.md:77 already loads this file at the plan-drafting step, so a citation resolves with no extra read). Per D1 AS SUPERSEDED by decision 132551fb: the plan CITES a playbook by name and anchor; it never transcribes the steps into plan.md. A skipped step stays visible and carries its recorded reason — it is NEVER a refusal, which is bee's existing named-deviation rule, not a new one.

The section opens with one line naming which taxonomy it binds: the ROUTE class (bee route --set --class), NOT the cell-level change_class enum at verbs/cells/validate.rs:123, which overlaps on bugfix and refactor only.

Four playbooks, each a short named step list:

- perf — 1) capture a baseline with the real command or trace and record the number; 2) state the hypothesis; 3) change one thing; 4) re-measure the same way; 5) keep the win, discard the loss, and record both numbers. 'It feels faster' is not a result.
- bugfix — 1) reproduce the symptom on the real interface; 2) watch the repro FAIL before the fix; 3) find the mechanism, not the symptom; 4) fix it; 5) re-run the same reproduction on the same interface. Step 2's rule already has a home: CITE skills/bee-swarming/references/worker-details.md:33-35 ('red-before-green is craft, applied by judgment and enforced by review, not by flags'). Point AT it — do not copy it and do not edit that file, which keeps a cold execution worker from having to load a planning reference.
- refactor — 1) record existing behavior first (characterization test, snapshot, or equivalence script); 2) prove that record green on the UNCHANGED tree; 3) change structure in small steps; 4) the record stays green at every step; 5) a behavior change is not a refactor — it is a separate cell.
- research — 1) read-only: the outcome is an account, never a diff; 2) trace the runtime path, not just the file list; 3) name every source searched that came up EMPTY; 4) end with anchors a reader can open. Per D3 this is the investigation route; note in one line that nothing yet ENFORCES read-only, so the step is craft (backlog p-69bee217).

Then wire two pointers, each ONE line, neither a copy: (1) skills/bee-planning/SKILL.md at the Record line (:42) — the step that records the route also cites the matched class playbook into plan.md; (2) skills/bee-hive/references/scout-and-ticks.md beside the class enum line (:34) — point at the playbook section. Do NOT reword the anchor phrases that packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/tests/route_class_parity.rs reads; run that fence and read its failure if unsure. Run `bee dev regen` after touching skills/**.
acceptance: planning-reference.md carries one `## Class playbooks` section with all four playbooks. bee-planning/SKILL.md and scout-and-ticks.md each carry a one-line pointer, not a copy. worker-details.md is UNEDITED. route_class_parity passes. release-manifest --check passes after regen.
